summary.headline: Skipper Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.5% to a record INR1,310 crore, EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore, margin 10.7%; FY27 guided at 15% growth.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 4.5% YoY to a record INR1,310 crore, with EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore and margin expanding 60 bps to 10.7%. PAT rose 26% to INR56.5 crore, helped by lower finance costs and operating leverage; management said the INR433.5 crore preferential equity raise came in late July/early August and did not benefit Q1. Order book closed at a record above INR9,200 crore and Q1 inflows were about INR1,674 crore (call also cites INR1,600 crore). Management reiterated 15% FY27 revenue growth and said the year is H2-weighted, with Engineering (export-heavy) soft in Q1.

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR1,674 crore (INR1,600 crore cited later)

segments.name: Engineering (incl. export)
segments.commentary: Soft in Q1 on low export and domestic order intake in FY26 and customers deferring shipments due to high freight costs; management called it temporary. Export order inflow guided up more than 50% YoY, about INR1,100 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue muted versus last year's above INR500 crore run-rate due to commodity price volatility and trade destocking; management guides about 20% top-line growth for FY27 with some margin improvement.

segments.name: Infra (EPC services)
segments.commentary: Strong growth in Q1 and past two quarters; revenue of about INR250 crore over two quarters cited. Management expects higher growth in this segment for FY27. Order book of about INR1,800 crore is infra, roughly 25% of order inflow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%, reiterated despite Q1 growth of about 5%; management expects H2 weighting.
FY27 order inflow target of INR7,000 crore-plus, implying closing order book of INR10,000 crore-plus; about INR1,100 crore from exports.
Expects about INR5,000 crore of the INR9,200 crore order book to execute in FY27; orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.
FY27 finance cost expected at 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue after the fundraise.
Long-term aspirational EBITDA margin 12%; export share of order inflow targeted at 50% long term (about 15% in FY27, 20-25% next year per management).
Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes expected to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (a few months' deferment), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa.
Indian transmission bids expected at INR90,000-100,000 crore in FY27 vs INR50,000-60,000 crore TBCB bidding in FY26.
capex_capacity: 75,000 tonne capacity expansion to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (slight delay), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa; bulk of this capacity is export-focused.
Fundraise of INR433.5 crore via preferential equity; entire proceeds used for debt repayment per management.
Subsidiaries established in Brazil and UAE; US entity expected to become operational shortly.
Two 765 kV projects secured in Maharashtra from a reputed developer in Q1.
Legacy low-margin contracts now under 5% of order book, largely executing out this year.
demand_pricing: Steel spiked in Q1 but normalised to pre-February levels by May; aluminium also eased. Management said firm-price contracts carry buffers, variable-price contracts adjust monthly, and inventory build-up and partial hedging are used.

Export inflow hit by tariffs and Middle East geopolitics last year; management says export ordering has rebounded, with advanced talks in the US, Australia, and other developed markets; Europe slower pending approvals.
Export shipments being deferred by customers due to elevated shipping costs.
Order book by segment: about 75% T&D-related infra/EPC services versus 25% of total order book; Q1 inflow almost entirely T&D.
Biggest challenge cited: quality technical manpower; company takes about 200-250 graduate trainees annually.

qa_highlights.question: Is ordering picking up versus FY26, and what is the outlook for the Indian transmission market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ordering has picked up, bids are being finalised, and inflows should translate from Q2. It expects INR90,000-1,00,000 crore of Indian transmission bids in FY27 and said about 40% of the INR9 lakh crore pipeline has been bid so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the finance cost decline due to the fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Fundraise funds arrived late July or early August, so Q1 had no benefit; the decline came from working capital management and operating leverage. FY27 finance cost guided at 3.2%-3.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is export revenue lost or delayed, and which segment drives 15% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export ordering has not stopped and export order inflow should rise more than 50% YoY. The 15% growth is expected from all three segments, with Infra growing fastest; Q1 and Q2 are seasonally slow due to monsoon, West Bengal elections, and freight disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR9,200 crore order book executes by FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR5,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, with short-term orders adding to this. Orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Polymer revenue muted and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to commodity price volatility and trade destocking. It expects about 20% Polymer top-line growth in FY27 with margin improvement, and says growth will come from both volume and value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited legacy low-margin contracts rolling off, better new-contract quality, operating leverage, and commodity mitigation through firm/variable price mix, inventory and hedging. It called the expansion structural and aimed toward 12% long-term margin.

qa_highlights.question: Does the delay in capacity expansion affect the 15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said commissioning is deferred only by a few months to end of Q2, with no impact on the 15% target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Engineering soften while Infra jumped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Engineering is affected by weak FY26 export and domestic order intake plus shipment deferrals due to high freight costs; it called this temporary. Infra growth is from TBCB transmission EPC services, with no change in scope of work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 order inflow target, and what is the export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR7,000 crore-plus of FY27 order inflow, with about INR1,100 crore from exports (about 15% of inflow).
